- If sentiment shows strong negative signals (e.g., -1.00) in recent days, model should reduce forecast slope or avoid upward momentum.  
- If sentiment shows strong positive signals (e.g., 1.00) and forecast is rising, check for overshoot — cap upward trend after spike.  
- When true outcome shows sharp reversal from high peaks, model often overestimates continuation — apply mean reversion bias correction.  
- If forecast is trending upward but true outcome shows early decline, model may be lagging — adjust for early reversal in sentiment-driven drops.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model should avoid overfitting to recent highs — use smoother trend or lower volatility assumption.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 spikes followed by 0.00/0.25, model may be overreacting — dampen forecast after spike.  
- If true outcome shows early dip after forecast peak, model may be misaligned with sentiment — adjust for sentiment lag.
